description: This bar chart illustrates the difference in percentage points between two models, mBERT and XLM-R, across multiple layers. The horizontal axis represents the layer number, labeled “layer”, with categories ranging from 0 to 12, and is sorted in ascending order. The vertical axis is labeled “% point difference” and represents a linear scale ranging from -10 to 0, with tick labels at -2 point intervals. The chart consists of 13 light blue bars, each corresponding to a specific layer. The height of the bars indicates the percentage point difference; the bar for layer 0 is approximately -0.5, while the bar for layer 12 is approximately -2.3. The bar heights generally decrease from layer 0 to layer 4, then remain relatively consistent between layers 5 and 12. A second bar chart is presented below, illustrating the same metric but for a different model, “concat”. This chart also has a horizontal axis labeled “layer” ranging from 0 to 12, sorted in ascending order, and a vertical axis labeled “% point difference” with a linear scale from -10 to 0, with tick labels at -2 point intervals. This chart consists of 13 dark blue bars, with the bar for layer 0 being approximately 2.3 and the bar for layer 4 being approximately -1.7. The bar heights generally decrease from layer 0 to layer 4, then remain relatively consistent between layers 5 and 12. No bars are visually emphasized in either chart.
